To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel BODIPY-functionalized [2]rotacane was successfully designed and synthesized.
we have designed a novel multifunctional switchable [2]-rotaxane with a novel BODIPY functionalized [2]rotacane.

a novel multifunctional [2]rotacane containing a BODIPY fluorophore and its derivatives were prepared and the shuttling motion and photoinduced electron transfers were demonstrated by utilizing external stimuli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, characterization, and application of novel BODIPY-functionalized [2]rotaxes and threads, which may be used in the development of novel MIMs and smart materials.
the synthesis, characterization, and application of a multifunctional mechanically-interlocked molecular switchable [2]-rotaxane.
the design, synthesis, characterization, and application of a novel multifunctional [2]rotaxyne.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study is the first example of a mechanically interlocked switch with two molecular stations that is able to be controlled by acid/base and H2PO 4 (-) stimuli, which could open up the way for the design and construction of new smart molecular machines.
a novel [2]rotacane R4 was synthesized by CuAAC click chemistry and its optical molecular switches were successfully demonstrated by utilizing acid/base and H2PO 4 (-) as external stimuli.
the [2]rotaxeane R4 and its derivatives can be considered as a novel and multifunctional optical molecular switch and H2PO2(-) ion sensor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the [2]rotacane R4 and its derivative R2 are promising candidates for the design of multifunctional optical molecular switches and H2PO3(-) ion probes.
the MIMs could provide a promising platform to develop a new type of optical molecular switch and sensor for the detection of H+ and H2PO42(-) ions in biological systems.
the [2]rotaxyne system could be a novel and efficient platform for the construction of multifunctional molecular switches.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MIMs are an excellent tool to construct a multifunctional optical switch, which could be used in the future for a variety of applications, such as molecular sensors, logic gates, and optoelectronic devices.

the MIM-based molecular switches can be used to detect H2PO4- and HPO42- ions and the [2]rotacane-based molecular switches can act as a new class of fluorescent sensors for the detection of HPO42- in living cells.
the [2]rotacanes with BODIPY functionalized can be used for the detection of HPO42- and H2PO42- and can be used as a molecular switch.
